desc: Establish cut condition: strong connectivity ⟺ every cut k has a backward arc ⟺ for all k, π⁻¹([B_k]) ⊄ [W_k]
Derive chain inclusion-exclusion with product formula |∩E_r| = ∏(i − cap(i)); verified by hand (BWBWBW→3, BWBWBWBW→13, BBWWBBWW→20, BWBWBBWW→16)
Implement O(N) stack-based candidate solution (run factorials + constraint stack merge)

Validate stack candidate against brute force — FAILED massively (BBWWBBWW: fast=2 vs brute=20; sample 3: fast=0 vs 240792); brute and O(N²) sweep DP agree everywhere, confirming the cut-coverage model

Implement the O(m²) IE recurrence (DP_r = −fact(W_r) − Σ_{q<r} DP_q·fact(W_r − B_q)·invfact(W_q − B_q); answer = fact(N) + Σ_r DP_r·fact(N−B_r)·invfact(W_r−B_r)) — VALIDATED: 0 mismatches on exhaustive N≤4, 300 random each N=5..8, all 3 samples (240792 ✓)

Investigate simplifications: no cut-filtering (record-d / record-gap / plateau-last) is exact — all m bad cuts are essential in the worst case; kernel K(q,r) is not a 1D difference kernel in index space, but fact(W_r − B_q) is a difference kernel in value space → D&C NTT is the fast path
Implement the O(N log² N) divide-and-conquer NTT evaluation of the IE recurrence (A_q = DP_q·invfact(W_q−B_q) at index B_q; convolve with factorial kernel; read off at W_r)
Validate the NTT version against the O(m²) IE on exhaustive N≤5 and random N≤12; stress-test performance at N=2×10⁵ (worst case alternating string, m = N−1)
Handle edge cases (S starts with W or ends with B → 0; m = 0 → N!; N = 1), re-verify samples, then deliver final stdin/stdout code
